title: Colab weird behaviour and error when passing values from collate_fn to validation_step
body:
The same code that runs perfectly on my local machine (MacOS with Python3.7 and tested on an Ubuntu docker 18.04 with Python3.6.9) fails to run on colab.

It performs weirdly, calling the Dataset init() multiple times. However, it fails when the collate function that (correctly) returns (printed out the results) the following:
```
return x_tensor, x_lengths, y_tensor
```
get passed in the sanity check right at start in the ``validation_step``:
```
def validation_step(self, batch: tuple, batch_nb: int, *args, **kwargs) -> dict:
        x_tensor, x_lengths, y_tensor = batch <-- here it fails
        .. forward(x_tensor,x _lengths) .. etc.
```
with the error:
```
line 234, in validation_step
    x_tensor, x_lengths, y_tensor = batch
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
```
it actually just return the first value (x_tensor). I tried packing them in a dict from the collate function, but in the validation step ``batch`` comes to me just as the first key (as string!) from the dict created in collate_fn.

The environment is the same except the Python version (latest torch and lightning versions) across local runtime, docker ubuntu and colab. To ensure the same code is running on all machines, I'm doing just git clone, pip3 install -r requirements and python3 train.py. Am I missing something with Colab that's just not working? I can provide full code if needed.
author: dumitrescustefan

comments.body: Hi! thanks for your contribution!, great first issue!

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that fixes the data unpacking issue in the validation_step function on Google Colab
Compatibility between the collate_fn return values and how they're processed in validation_step
Consistent behavior between local development environment and Google Colab

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

--- ./pl_examples/multi_node_examples/README.md ---
# Multi-node example   

This demo launches a job using 2 GPUs on 2 different nodes (4 GPUs total).
To run this demo do the following:

1. Log into the jumphost node of your SLURM-managed cluster.  
2. Create a conda environment with Lightning and a GPU PyTorch version.   
3. Choose a script to submit    

#### DDP  
Submit this job to run with distributedDataParallel (2 nodes, 2 gpus each)
```bash
sbatch ddp_job_submit.sh YourEnv
```

#### DDP2  
Submit this job to run with a different implementation of distributedDataParallel.
In this version, each node acts like DataParallel but syncs across nodes like DDP.
```bash
sbatch ddp2_job_submit.sh YourEnv
```

# Basic Examples   
Use these examples to test how lightning works.

```

---

```   

---

Train on multiple GPUs using DataParallel.

```bash
python gpu_template.py --gpus 2 --distributed_backend dp
```   

---
#### DistributedDataParallel (ddp)    

Train on multiple GPUs using DistributedDataParallel   
```bash
python gpu_template.py --gpus 2 --distributed_backend ddp
```

---
#### DistributedDataParallel+DP (ddp2)    

Train on multiple GPUs using DistributedDataParallel + dataparallel.
On a single node, uses all GPUs for 1 model. Then shares gradient information
across nodes.   
```bash
python gpu_template.py --gpus 2 --distributed_backend ddp2
```

FROM python:3.7

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    wget \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone the repository and checkout the specific commit
RUN git clone https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning.git . && \
    git checkout 3be81cb54ebf2b5425cae09327e852bea0e7c492

# Install PyTorch (using a version compatible with the commit timeframe)
# Using a version that was common around the time of this commit
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir torch==1.4.0 torchvision==0.5.0

# Install project dependencies
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Install optional dependencies that might be needed for the issue
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements-extra.txt

# Install the project in development mode
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -e .

# Create a workspace directory for users to mount their code
RUN mkdir -p /workspace

# Add a README with information about the issue
RUN echo "# PyTorch Lightning Issue #1221 Environment\n\n" \
    "This container provides an environment to reproduce and fix the issue where\n" \
    "collate_fn values are not properly passed to validation_step.\n\n" \
    "The issue appears to be related to how batch data is handled during validation.\n\n" \
    "To test your fix, you can modify the code and run your tests in this environment.\n" > /workspace/README.md

# Set the working directory for user code
WORKDIR /workspace
